systems.title: 5-Minute Grab-and-Go Bag
systems.description: A compact bag kept where it can be accessed when leaving. It is designed to move with you, not to replace other household supplies. Tailor contents and carrying arrangements to each person’s needs.

systems.title: 15-Minute Ready Duffel
systems.description: A larger portable kit for time away from home. Consider the needs of every household member, including infants, older adults, people with disabilities, medically dependent people and pets. Contents and quantities depend on individual circumstances and current official guidance.

systems.title: 20-Minute Vehicle OR Suitcase Prep
systems.description: Choose the path that matches your situation. Vehicle supplies stay secured in the vehicle; suitcase supplies are portable and travel with the household. Do not treat the two paths as one combined packing task.

systems.title: 60-Minute Home Resilience
systems.description: A focused home setup for sheltering in place, leaving safely and managing disruptions. Local hazards, building type, household needs and official instructions determine what is appropriate.

systems.title: Off-Grid Systems
systems.description: Pro add-on. This checklist identifies low-tech backup supplies and resources. Consult utilities, manufacturers and qualified professionals about suitability, safety and installation.

systems.title: Water Purification
systems.description: Pro add-on. This checklist covers household water planning and identifies authoritative resources. No single filter or treatment method makes every water source safe. Consult current CDC and EPA guidance, local health advisories and product manufacturers.

systems.title: Home Battery & Solar
systems.description: Pro add-on. Identify essential devices and discuss backup options with equipment manufacturers, healthcare providers and qualified electrical professionals. Do not rely on this checklist for electrical sizing or configuration.

systems.title: Emergency Cooling / Heat Resilience
systems.description: Pro add-on. Extreme heat can become dangerous even indoors. Identify safe cooling resources, transportation options and emergency contacts. Confusion, fainting, or very high body temperature is a medical emergency. Call 911 and follow the dispatcher's instructions.

systems.title: Long-Term Food
systems.description: Pro add-on. Build a rotating pantry from foods the household already eats. Pantry planning should reflect household needs, storage space, budget, dietary requirements and local conditions; no single duration is appropriate for every household.

Have a manual communication backup, including a paper contact list and radio; consult official emergency-management resources about household communication planning.
For alternative cooking equipment, consult the manufacturer, local fire authority and official fire-safety resources about suitability and restrictions.
For fuel-related safety, storage, handling and maintenance questions, consult the equipment manufacturer and local fire authority. This checklist does not provide fuel procedures.
Consult the cookware and appliance manufacturers about compatibility.
Have working carbon-monoxide alarms and keep emergency contacts accessible; consult the manufacturer and local fire authority about alarm requirements.

Have accessible fire-safety equipment. Evacuate first. Use an extinguisher only on a small, contained fire when you have a clear exit behind you. Know where it is and when to leave instead. Consult the local fire authority or a recognized training provider.
Have laundry supplies suited to household needs; consult local public-health guidance about sanitation during utility interruptions.
Have dishwashing and sanitation supplies suited to household needs; consult current public-health guidance for specific requirements.
Have a household security plan and consult local public-safety resources; do not rely on improvised traps or hazards.
Have emergency sanitation supplies and consult local public-health authorities about sanitation and waste-disposal guidance.
Consider household water needs, pets, health needs, storage capacity and local conditions. Consult current local emergency and public-health guidance; do not rely on a universal quantity or duration.

items.text: Use food-grade containers designed for water
items.description: Identify containers intended for drinking-water storage and review manufacturer and public-health guidance about suitability.

items.text: Store water in a cool, dark location
items.description: Consult the water-container manufacturer and public-health authorities about appropriate storage conditions.
Keep an inventory of stored water and relevant product or source information.
Have a suitable dispensing option; consult the container manufacturer and public-health authorities about safe handling.
Identify and clearly distinguish drinking-water and non-drinking-water supplies using appropriate labels and records.
Consult current manufacturer and public-health guidance about stored-water inspection and replacement.

items.text: Water filter research and product information
items.description: Research filters with independently documented performance for contaminants of concern. Consult current CDC/EPA guidance and product manufacturers; filter capabilities vary.
Consult current CDC and EPA guidance, local public-health authorities and product manufacturers about source-specific water treatment options.
Keep current CDC, EPA and local public-health guidance available for emergency drinking-water decisions.
Keep links to current CDC/EPA guidance and product information for drinking-water safety. Do not include chemical concentrations, dosage or contact-time instructions.

Do not use household bleach or other chemicals for drinking-water treatment based on this checklist. Consult current CDC/EPA guidance and local public-health authorities for source-specific information.
Consult current public-health guidance about water with visible sediment; appearance alone does not establish that water is safe.

Do not assume water suspected of fuel, toxic chemical, heavy-metal or radioactive contamination can be made safe by ordinary boiling or disinfection. Contact local public-health authorities and consult current CDC/EPA guidance.
Have clear labels and records to distinguish drinking-water supplies from untreated or non-potable sources.

items.text: Never dip used cups or hands into stored drinking water
items.description: Consult the container manufacturer and public-health authorities about protecting stored drinking water from contamination.

items.text: Clean and sanitize containers before refilling
items.description: Consult current public-health guidance and container manufacturer information about cleaning and preparing water containers.
Keep a record of water sources, relevant advisories and products; consult public-health authorities for treatment decisions.
Consult container manufacturers and local public-health authorities about stored-water inspection and replacement.
Consult the water-heater manufacturer, utility or qualified professional about whether stored water may be available; do not attempt access procedures based on this checklist.

items.text: Freezer ice as a reserve only when known clean
items.description: Consider alternative water sources only when their safety is established by current public-health guidance or an appropriate authority.
Consult local rules and public-health guidance before considering rainwater as a water source; do not assume collected water is suitable for drinking.
Never walk, swim, or drive through floodwater. Do not use floodwater or contaminated runoff as drinking water. Consult local public-health authorities and official water advisories.
After flooding, consult the local health department and qualified well professionals about testing and any required follow-up before relying on private-well water.
Identify official drinking-water distribution points, approved bottled-water sources and local advisories.
Include medical equipment, communications, lighting, refrigeration and any critical accessibility equipment.
Record device names and manufacturer information; consult equipment providers and qualified professionals about electrical requirements.
Identify essential device power needs with the equipment manufacturer, healthcare provider and a qualified electrical professional; do not calculate or assume capacity from this checklist.
Prioritize life-sustaining medical needs, communications, lighting and other essential services.
List comfort and convenience devices that can be paused.
Discuss medical-device continuity, backup options, supplier contacts and alternate care arrangements with the healthcare provider and equipment manufacturer.
Consult equipment manufacturers and a qualified electrical professional about whether a battery or power station is suitable for the intended household needs.
Review manufacturer documentation and consult a qualified electrical professional about compatibility with intended devices.

items.text: Check battery chemistry and operating limits
items.description: Consult the manufacturer about battery chemistry, operating limits, charging, storage and safety notices.
Consult the manufacturer about safe power-bank care and what to do with damaged or recalled units.
Keep required adapters with each device.
Consult the manufacturer about recommended battery inspection, maintenance and replacement; this checklist does not provide maintenance procedures.
Keep digital and printed copies accessible.
Consult the power-station and solar-panel manufacturers or a qualified installer about compatibility and approved equipment.
Consult manufacturer documentation and a qualified installer about appropriate solar equipment placement and installation.

items.text: Account for shade, clouds and short winter days
items.description: Consult the solar and power-station manufacturers or a qualified installer about expected performance under local conditions.

items.text: Use only approved cables and adapters
items.description: Use only manufacturer-approved equipment; consult the manufacturer or qualified installer about cable and adapter compatibility.

items.text: Protect equipment from weather and theft
items.description: Follow the manufacturer’s operating and storage instructions.
Consult manufacturer instructions and a qualified electrical professional about appropriate charging arrangements.
Consult the manufacturer and qualified service providers about inspection, maintenance or damaged electrical equipment.

items.text: Electrical system compatibility and professional advice
items.description: Consult the equipment manufacturer and a qualified electrician about safe system compatibility and configuration.
Follow the provider’s backup-power guidance.

items.text: Qualified electrician consultation for home integration
items.description: Consult a licensed electrician about any home electrical integration or backup-power connection. Do not attempt electrical modifications based on this checklist.

items.text: Generator safety information and professional guidance
items.description: Never run a generator, grill, camp stove, or charcoal indoors, in a garage, or in any enclosed space. For other generator safety topics, consult current manufacturer, utility, fire-authority and official carbon-monoxide safety guidance.
Identify carbon-monoxide alarms and review manufacturer and local fire-authority guidance about placement, maintenance and replacement.
For generator fuel storage and handling, consult the generator manufacturer and local fire authority. This checklist does not provide fuel procedures.

For generator refueling and maintenance, consult the generator manufacturer, local fire authority and qualified service professionals. This checklist does not provide operating or refueling procedures.

items.text: Generator weather and electrical safety information
items.description: Review manufacturer and official safety guidance about weather exposure and electrical hazards; consult qualified professionals when needed.
Consult the generator manufacturer, a qualified electrician and applicable electrical requirements about compatible electrical accessories.

items.text: Generator maintenance and professional service information
items.description: For generator maintenance, consult the manufacturer and qualified service professionals. This checklist does not provide maintenance, operating or shutdown procedures.
Consider shade, lower heat gain and safe airflow.
Know local cooling centers, public facilities and transport options.

items.text: Create a heat alert and check-in plan
items.description: Monitor official forecasts and check on higher-risk people at agreed intervals.
Consider household hydration needs and discuss individual fluid restrictions or medical concerns with a healthcare provider. Consult official public-health guidance during heat events.
Have cooling supplies appropriate to household needs; consult official public-health guidance about heat-related health concerns. This checklist does not provide cooling treatment methods.

items.text: Lightweight, loose clothing and sun protection
items.description: Include hats and shade for outdoor exposure.
Consult official public-health and local emergency-management guidance about reducing indoor heat exposure.

items.text: Official heat-health information and emergency contacts
items.description: Confusion, fainting, or very high body temperature is a medical emergency. Call 911 and follow the dispatcher's instructions. Keep current official public-health information and emergency contacts accessible.

items.text: Battery or USB fan for limited use
items.description: Treat as supplemental comfort, not a solution to dangerous indoor heat.

items.text: Power budget for fans and medical devices
items.description: Identify devices that may need backup power and consult equipment manufacturers and qualified electrical professionals about options.
Consult official weather, air-quality and local safety guidance about ventilation during extreme weather or smoke events.
Have suitable window coverings; consult local safety guidance and ensure household exits and required ventilation remain accessible.
Consolidate activity only if the room remains safe and accessible.
Consult official air-quality alerts and local public-health guidance when making decisions about outdoor air and ventilation.

items.text: List medications affected by heat or refrigeration
items.description: Ask a pharmacist, prescriber or medication manufacturer about medication storage requirements during heat or power interruptions.
Keep appliance and food-safety manufacturer information and current official food-safety guidance available for outage decisions.
Discuss approved storage options with the pharmacist, prescriber and medication manufacturer; do not improvise cooling or storage methods.
Identify essential medical devices and discuss backup power and continuity options with the healthcare provider, equipment manufacturer and qualified electrical professional.

items.text: Emergency contacts for pharmacies and suppliers
items.description: Include after-hours contacts and refill options.
Identify who can assist with transport or supplies.
Stage enough for everyone, including infants and people with limited mobility.
Identify suitable warming resources and consult equipment manufacturers, local fire authorities and qualified professionals about heating safety.
Keep official fire and carbon-monoxide safety resources available for information about combustion equipment. This checklist does not provide appliance operating instructions.
Identify carbon-monoxide alarms and review manufacturer and local fire-authority guidance about placement, maintenance and replacement.
Consult local utility and public-authority guidance about freeze preparedness and household water systems; consult qualified professionals about utility or plumbing work.
Know where to go before conditions become unsafe.

items.text: Estimate daily food needs for each household member
items.description: Consider household members’ ages, activity, medical needs, allergies and dietary restrictions when organizing food supplies. Consult qualified professionals for individualized nutrition questions.
Consider a pantry goal that reflects household needs, budget, storage capacity, dietary requirements and local conditions; no single duration is appropriate for every household.

items.text: Ready-to-eat food supplies for household needs
items.description: Consider keeping ready-to-eat foods that suit household needs and do not depend on cooking equipment; choose supplies based on individual circumstances.

items.text: Account for allergies and medical diets
items.description: Keep safe substitutes and clear labels.

items.text: Include infants, children and older adults
items.description: Use age-appropriate foods and familiar textures.
Plan pet food and related supplies according to each animal’s needs; consult a veterinarian about special diets, medications or health concerns.

items.text: Plan water and fuel alongside food
items.description: Consider water and cooking-energy needs alongside food supplies; consult official preparedness guidance for household-specific planning.
Rice, oats, pasta, flour or other familiar staples stored dry and pest-proof.
Dried or canned beans, lentils, nut butters, fish or meats suited to household preferences.
Bring cooking oils and fats that suit household needs; consult product labeling for storage information.
Bring salt, sugar and seasonings suited to household needs.
Choose products that meet dietary needs and storage conditions.
Choose familiar foods and rotate.
Include coffee, tea, chocolate or child favorites where appropriate.

items.text: Special diet and medical nutrition products
items.description: Follow clinician guidance and product storage instructions.

items.text: Date packages when purchased or opened
items.description: Have an inventory of food supplies and relevant product information.
Consult current official food-safety guidance about food dates and discarding damaged, spoiled or unsafe food.
Have food-safe storage containers; consult food-safety guidance and product manufacturers about suitability.
Keep a pantry inventory that reflects household needs, dietary coverage and available supplies.

items.text: Practice one preservation method before relying on it
items.description: For home food preservation, consult tested, authoritative food-safety resources and qualified extension or food-safety professionals. This checklist does not provide preservation procedures.
Consult current official food-safety guidance and appliance manufacturer information when assessing food after an outage.

items.text: Keep non-food chemicals away from food
items.description: Keep non-food chemicals separate from food and water; consult product labels and local hazardous-material guidance for storage questions.

items.text: Small seed kit for foods the household eats
items.description: Bring seeds for foods the household uses; consult local extension or gardening resources about suitable varieties.

items.text: Hand tools for garden or patio growing
items.description: Have garden or patio tools suited to household needs; consult product information for safe use and storage.
Consult local public-health and gardening guidance about non-potable water; do not divert drinking water needed for people or pets.
Have manual food-preparation tools suited to household needs; consult product information for safe use.
Have food-preparation and hygiene supplies; consult current public-health guidance about handwashing, clean surfaces and safe water.
